solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Hail showers not new during exercise

indicators.note: during says one piece sits within the span of the other, here inside the exercise letters

parts.note: PE is physical exercise, school gym lessons

indicators.note: not tells us the letter for new is dropped from the showers word

parts.note: showers as a verb: it rains

explanation.surface: A complaint that a hailstorm came down while people were doing physical exercise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hail' looks like weather to match 'showers', but it is the verb of acclaim.
explanation.definitionFit: To hail someone is to acclaim or laud them, so both verbs mean commend highly.

clue.text: Eden Project's initial publicity seen in spring

indicators.note: initial means just the first letter of project
seen in places the publicity word inside the spring word

parts.note: to spring up is to arise
an ad is an advert, publicity

explanation.surface: Cornwall's Eden Project got its early publicity in springtime.
explanation.walkthrough: The Eden Project is a Cornish visitor attraction of giant plant domes; here 'Eden' is the biblical garden.
explanation.definitionFit: The Garden of Eden in Genesis is the original idyllic paradise.

clue.text: Blue Toyota scratching parking sign

parts.note: aqua is a light blue colour

indicators.note: scratching means crossing out, so the parking letter is removed

parts.note: the Prius is a Toyota hybrid car
P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking

explanation.surface: A blue Toyota scrapes a parking sign.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scratching' removes P from PRIUS to leave RIUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Aquarius is the eleventh sign of the zodiac, the water carrier.

clue.text: Cream dish British friend brought up, covered by sandwich

indicators.note: covered by puts the reversed piece within the sandwich word

parts.note: a sub is a submarine sandwich

indicators.note: brought up in a down clue means read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: an ally is a friend

explanation.surface: A British friend brings along a creamy pudding and a sandwich.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'brought up' reverses the friend and British letters before they go in.
explanation.definitionFit: Syllabub is an old English dessert of whipped cream with wine and sugar.

clue.text: Carrying two matching keys, postie wavered outside the box

indicators.note: carrying means the scrambled postie letters hold the keys within them
wavered suggests unsteady movement, so the letters of postie are shuffled

parts.note: two identical musical keys: F and F

explanation.surface: A wobbly postman, keys in hand, strays outside the mailbox.
explanation.walkthrough: 'two matching keys' are musical keys, both F; 'Carrying' puts them inside the shuffled postie letters, just after the first.
explanation.definitionFit: Off-piste figuratively means departing from the usual route, like unconventional thinking beyond normal limits.

clue.text: Hair disturbance — a feature of grandad's head?

parts.note: fur is animal hair
a row is a noisy disturbance

explanation.surface: An old man's hair gets ruffled.
explanation.definitionFit: A furrow is a deep wrinkle, as on an older person's brow; the question mark flags the example.

clue.text: Social training jog

parts.note: a prom is a school dance, a social
PT is physical training

explanation.surface: A sociable run organised as part of fitness training.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jog' is the memory-jogging sense, not running.
explanation.definitionFit: To prompt someone is to jog their memory or nudge them into action.

clue.text: Mum loves wearing a certain thing

parts.note: sh is the call for quiet, keeping mum
love is zero in tennis, so two loves are OO
wearing clothes means being in them

explanation.surface: Mother loves wearing one particular garment.
explanation.definitionFit: A shoo-in is a certainty, especially a candidate sure to win.

clue.text: Drug injected into breed of cattle heading off somewhere in Devon

indicators.note: injected into puts the drug letter inside the trimmed cattle word
heading off removes the first letter of the cattle breed

parts.note: the Dexter is a small Irish breed of cattle
E is the abbreviation for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A vet injects a cow before it is moved on, somewhere in Devon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading off' strips D from DEXTER, and 'injected into' inserts E to give EX-E-TER.
explanation.definitionFit: Exeter is the county town of Devon, in south-west England.

clue.text: Don't start to bother with foreign currency

indicators.note: don't start tells us to remove the opening letter of the word for bother

parts.note: trouble means bother, fuss or difficulty

explanation.surface: Advice not to fuss about changing money abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Don't start to' removes the T from TROUBLE.
explanation.definitionFit: The rouble is the monetary unit of Russia, a currency from abroad for a British solver.

clue.text: Criminal to score Ecstasy, covering for fence

indicators.note: criminal suggests something crooked, so the letters of to score are rearranged

parts.note: E is the street abbreviation for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A crook out to buy Ecstasy, with a fence (a receiver of stolen goods) as front.
explanation.walkthrough: A fence is also slang for a dealer in stolen goods, which the surface plays on; here it is a garden fence.
explanation.definitionFit: Creosote is a tarry wood preservative painted over garden fencing as a protective coat.

clue.text: Headwear daughter preferred over time, somewhere in Africa

indicators.note: preferred over means one letter is chosen instead of another, a swap

parts.note: a turban is a wrapped head covering

explanation.surface: A girl choosing which hat to wear over the years.
explanation.walkthrough: 'preferred over' swaps the T of TURBAN for D.
explanation.definitionFit: Durban is a major port city on the east coast of South Africa.

clue.text: Second run by husband in wood needing painkiller

parts.note: a mo is a moment, a second
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

indicators.note: in places the husband letter inside the wood word

parts.note: pine is a softwood timber

explanation.surface: A runner hurts himself among the trees and quickly needs pain relief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Second' is a moment, not second place.
explanation.definitionFit: Morphine is an opiate drug given to relieve severe pain.

clue.text: Aristocrat to drive up with half-cut collaborator

indicators.note: up in a down clue means read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: to ram is to drive forcibly

indicators.note: half-cut keeps only the first half of the collaborator word

parts.note: a quisling is a traitor who collaborates with an occupying enemy

explanation.surface: A drunken toff drives off with a turncoat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' gives MAR from RAM; 'half-cut' takes QUIS from QUISLING. Half-cut is also slang for drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: A marquis is a nobleman ranking above an earl or count.

clue.text: Soldier and wife like carpaccio?

parts.note: RA is the Royal Artillery, so a gunner or soldier

explanation.surface: A couple wonder whether their dish resembles carpaccio.
explanation.definitionFit: Carpaccio is thinly sliced uncooked beef, so the dish is an example of uncooked food; the question mark flags the example.

clue.text: Mum finding slug around shed

indicators.note: around says the drink word wraps round the shed word

parts.note: a slug is a gulp of drink; to sup is to drink
a hut is a small shed

explanation.surface: Mother discovers a slug crawling about the garden shed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mum' is not mother but the call for silence, as in 'keep mum'.
explanation.definitionFit: Mum as an interjection demands silence, the same instruction as the blunter two-word command.

clue.text: Italian runner cross, getting ailment

parts.note: the Po is Italy's longest river; rivers run
X is the shape of a cross

explanation.surface: An irritable Italian athlete comes down with something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'runner' is a river, not an athlete.
explanation.definitionFit: Pox is a general name for diseases with pustules, such as smallpox.

clue.text: King's Head, say, where this vessel is seen?

indicators.note: head means the first letter of the word king

parts.note: say means for example, abbreviated eg

explanation.surface: The King's Head, for instance, is a pub where a beer barrel would be found.
explanation.walkthrough: The King's Head is a common British pub name, and a keg holds beer there.
explanation.definitionFit: A keg is a small barrel, a container for beer.

clue.text: Nose that Parisian caught in fight

indicators.note: caught in means the French word is held inside the fight word

parts.note: a bout is a boxing contest
que is French for that, as a Parisian would say it

explanation.surface: A Parisian's nose gets hurt in a scrap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nose' is the wine-tasting sense, not the facial feature.
explanation.definitionFit: A wine's nose and its bouquet are both the aroma a taster sniffs from the glass.

clue.text: Music player misinterpreted note, admitting memory blank at intro

indicators.note: admitting means letting the memory and blank letters inside the rearranged note
misinterpreted means read wrongly, so the letters of note are rearranged

parts.note: ROM is read-only memory in computing

indicators.note: at intro takes only the opening letter of blank

explanation.surface: A musician misreads a note and goes blank on the opening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'misinterpreted' turns note into TONE, and 'admitting' takes the memory letters plus B ('at intro' of blank) after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A trombone is a brass instrument; 'player' here is the thing played.

clue.text: Mythical island's last building houses opponent

indicators.note: houses means the opponent word is held inside the rearranged letters
building means putting together, so the letters of last are rearranged

parts.note: someone anti is against, an opponent

explanation.surface: The final structure on a legendary island accommodates an enemy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'building' rearranges LAST into ATLS, which 'houses' ANTI. The 's stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Atlantis is Plato's legendary island said to have sunk beneath the sea.

clue.text: Expert with file perhaps hosting carbon convention

parts.note: a pro is a professional, an expert

indicators.note: hosting means the carbon letter is held inside the tool word

parts.note: a file is an example of a tool
C is the chemical symbol for carbon

explanation.surface: A specialist with a dossier holds a climate conference on carbon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'file' is the metal tool, not a dossier.
explanation.definitionFit: A protocol is an accepted code of procedure or etiquette, a convention.

clue.text: Culinary device right behind jar

indicators.note: behind puts the right letter after the jar word

parts.note: to jar or grate is to jangle the nerves

explanation.surface: A kitchen gadget positioned to the right of a jar on the shelf.
explanation.definitionFit: A grater is a kitchen tool for shredding cheese or vegetables.

clue.text: Dirty film, mainly vacuous

parts.note: scum is a film of dirt on a liquid's surface

indicators.note: vacuous means empty, so mainly loses its inside letters

explanation.surface: A grubby movie that is largely empty-headed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vacuous' empties mainly to MY.
explanation.definitionFit: Scummy means covered in grime or, figuratively, contemptible and squalid.

clue.text: Thespian's posh verses found in fiction

indicators.note: found in places the posh and verses letters within the fiction word

parts.note: a lie is a fiction, an untruth
U means upper-class, posh
V is verse, so VV is verses

explanation.surface: An actor's refined poetry appears in a novel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found in' puts U and VV inside LIE. The 's stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A luvvie is a jokey British term for an effusive, theatrical actor.

clue.text: Found the net small, getting fish around banks of Ribble

indicators.note: around means the fish word goes round the river's edge letters

parts.note: cod is a fish

indicators.note: banks of takes the outside letters of Ribble, as a river has banks

explanation.surface: An angler on the River Ribble lands a small fish in the net.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ribble is a river in north-west England; 'net' is the football goal, not an angler's.
explanation.definitionFit: To find the net is football idiom for scoring a goal.

clue.text: Verb is described in other words

parts.note: V is the grammatical abbreviation for verb

indicators.note: described here means spoken, so is is written as it is pronounced

parts.note: the word is, pronounced with a z sound

explanation.surface: A grammar note: the verb 'is' gets explained using different wording.
explanation.walkthrough: 'described' signals that IS is written the way it is pronounced, IZ.
explanation.definitionFit: Viz, from Latin videlicet, means namely, introducing a restatement or clarification.

clue.text: Bull's eye by Charlie in lead bomber

indicators.note: in puts the middle and Charlie letters inside the lead word

parts.note: the van is the lead, the front position

indicators.note: eye is the centre, as in the eye of a storm, so take the middle of bull

parts.note: C is Charlie in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A darts player hits the bullseye beside Charlie, the top scorer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eye' means the centre, as in the eye of a storm, so it takes the middle of Bull.
explanation.definitionFit: The Vulcan was a British delta-wing strategic jet bomber of the Cold War.

clue.text: Liverpudlian, contracted to put on company uniform, steamed wheat

indicators.note: to put on means the shortened word is attached after the company and uniform letters

parts.note: U is uniform in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: contracted means shortened, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a Scouse is a person from Liverpool

explanation.surface: A Liverpudlian signs a contract to wear a firm's uniform.
explanation.walkthrough: 'contracted' misleads as signing a contract; it means shortened by a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Couscous is semolina of durum wheat, steamed and served as a North African staple.

clue.text: One changes pronunciation in spiritual music retrospective

indicators.note: retrospective says the hidden letters are read backwards
in tells us the answer sits inside the run of words spiritual music

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A look back at a gospel singer whose pronunciation changes.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft left 'in' unassigned, but it is what signals the hiding, so it is named as the hidden-word indicator here.
explanation.definitionFit: An umlaut is the two-dot accent in German that alters a vowel's sound.

clue.text: State probes motorway, with check at borders to find rebel

indicators.note: probes means the state word pushes into the motorway letters

parts.note: the M1 is a British motorway, written MI
to aver is to state firmly

indicators.note: at borders takes only the outside letters of check

explanation.surface: A government agency investigates a motorway, with checkpoints at the borders, to catch a dissident.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is England's main north-south motorway; its 1 is read as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: A maverick is an independent-minded nonconformist, a free-thinking dissenter.

clue.text: Moments occasionally in film expressed figuratively

indicators.note: in places the selected letters inside the film word

parts.note: a pic is a picture, a film

indicators.note: occasionally means taking only every other letter of moments

explanation.surface: A cinema-goer remembers only scattered scenes from a film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'occasionally' takes the second, fourth and sixth letters of Moments.
explanation.definitionFit: Poetic language uses imagery and metaphor rather than literal statement.

clue.text: After year one, uninitiated male horse's compliant

indicators.note: after says the trimmed horse word comes following year and one

parts.note: the Roman numeral I is one

indicators.note: uninitiated means without the first letter

parts.note: a gelding is a castrated male horse

explanation.surface: After its first year, a young male horse becomes docile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uninitiated' strips G from GELDING; 'After' puts ELDING behind Y and I. The 's stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Yielding describes someone giving way readily, submissive and accommodating.

clue.text: Shark wanted, in essence, owed cash — help!

indicators.note: in essence means taking the heart, the middle letters, of each word that follows

explanation.surface: A desperate debtor cries for help, pursued by a loan shark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in essence' takes the central pair of each of owed, cash and help. 'wanted' only links, telling us the definition is wanted.
explanation.definitionFit: Weasel and shark are both slang for a sly, untrustworthy, predatory person.
